subject: SLO exception request — Nebula Health launch: throughput & queueing fallback
messages:
From: Aisha Mirza <aisha.mirza@nebulahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nebulahealth.com, ops@nebulahealth.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity SLA carveout for teletriage launch

Rachel —

Thanks for taking a look. We're planning a public launch for Nebula's teletriage product on 2027-07-10 and are putting the final pieces together for inference capacity. Our legal and ops teams are asking for a carveout to the standard Dedicated SLA because of the expected burst shape and the strict latency tail we need for real-time voice/agent assist. High-level ask:

- Sustained ingest peak: ~9k–12k tokens/sec for 10–12s bursts, expected once per minute during peak 1 hour windows (US east).
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 120ms for generate calls when routed to dedicated pool (user-facing).
- Queueing behavior: requests should not be re-queued > 200ms during contention; we need guaranteed routing to reserved GPUs for priority traffic.
- Fallbacks: we need a documented fallback policy (model shard, quantized variant) and clear operational steps when reserved pool reaches capacity.

Attached: Nebula_SLA_ask_v1.pdf, launch_plan.xlsx. Can Redwood provide a written exception/addendum outlining queueing semantics, headroom guarantees, and any crediting policy if the carveout is missed?

We can jump on a call today if helpful — procurement and SRE are on copy.

Thanks,
Aisha Mirza
Head of Platform Partnerships
Nebula Health Systems

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Mirza <aisha.mirza@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity SLA carveout for teletriage launch

Aisha —

Appreciate the detail and congrats on the upcoming launch. I've pulled in Ben (inference infra) and Laura (commercial) to scope the ask. Initial notes / clarifying questions:

- Traffic profile: can you share a 24h sample (CSV) with per-second qps and sequence length distribution? The burst cadence matters for our autoscaling and headroom math.
- Reserved pool sizing: given the 9k–12k tokens/s, we need to know your preferred reserved GPU count (we can propose a configuration).
- Latency SLO: we typically measure token-generation latency and end-to-end response time on 1-minute windows; we can discuss moving to a 5-minute measurement window for this addendum.

Mitigations we can offer while we scope the contract addendum:
- Short-term: enable a 30% burst buffer on top of reserved capacity for the launch week and configure route-level priority for teletriage traffic.
- Fallback: automatic fallback to a half-precision quantized variant of the model with a documented ~12% quality delta and ~2x token/s throughput improvement (we'll log any fallback events).
- Runbook: we'll provide a runbook that includes preemption rules, queueing thresholds, and on-call escalation steps.

I've attached our redwood-capacity-playbook.pdf for your SREs — it covers queueing semantics and preemption rules. Ben: can you review the latency measurement options and suggest a headroom setting that maps to their burst profile?

If procurement wants a concrete draft addendum, Laura can prepare a 1-page SLA addendum and proposed credit schedule.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference

Rachel / team —

Quick technical readout after reviewing Aisha's attachments and our capacity tests:

- Queueing model: Dedicated pools are isolated but subject to shared host-level interrupts. We can enforce tenant-level concurrency slots plus a soft headroom policy. For Nebula's profile I recommend: guaranteed-concurrency=40 (per-pool), headroom=20% above forecast sustained throughput, and burst-reserve=1.5x for windows <= 15s.
- Measurement window: switch SLA windows to 5-minute rolling windows for latency and 1-minute peak windows for throughput alerts. This reduces noise for short spikes.
- Preemption rules: priority traffic mapped to reserved GPUs will preempt best-effort workloads in the same host group; preemption latency is typically <100ms but we must document worst-case tail behavior (up to ~400ms) for software-level KV cache eviction under extreme scenarios.
- Crediting: propose a crediting formula: incident credit = min(10% monthly invoice, (breach_duration_minutes / total_billed_minutes) * monthly_fee). We should limit to 30% cap per month.

Attachments: throughput-math.csv (capacity sizing examples with token/sec to GPU conversions).

I'll join any call with their SREs — we should also offer an initial capacity shakedown run (3 days) prior to launch with routing directed to the dedicated pool.

— Ben
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick turn. Summary of agreed path forward and asks from Nebula so we can get the addendum signed:

1) Commercial pilot: 6-month SLA addendum (Laura will put the doc in DocuSign). Remedies: 10% credit for first two incidents each month, 15% subsequently, cap 30%/month.

2) Technical guardrails (Ben's recommendations accepted): guaranteed-concurrency=40, headroom=20%, burst-reserve=1.5x for <=15s bursts. Measurement windows: latency=5m rolling (95th), throughput=1m peak. Preemption and queueing semantics are documented in the runbook.

3) Operational commitments:
- Runbook & telemetry: Redwood will deliver the runbook and daily telemetry dashboards during launch week.
- Pre-launch shakedown: schedule a 72-hour stress test targeting your expected peak profile; Ben will lead.
- Fallback behavior: automatic fallback to quantized model variant when queueing thresholds are hit; fallback events will be logged and visible in the console.

4) Action items for Nebula (please confirm):
- Share the 24h sample traffic CSV (per-second qps + seq length distributions).
- Confirm reserved GPU target (recommendation attached: see throughput-math.csv).
- Procurement to review DocuSign link and circulate.

Attachments included for reference: Nebula_SLA_ask_v1.pdf; redwood-capacity-playbook.pdf; throughput-math.csv; Nebula-SOW-v2.docx.

Proposed kickoff: 2027-06-25 10:00 AM ET for a joint runbook walk. If that works, Laura will finalize the DocuSign and Ben will schedule the engineering prep.

Best regards,
Rachel Kim
